utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, you may be seated. Good morning to you all. Madam registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-97-24-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, Susan Somers, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You, Your Honour, Susan L. Somers for the prosecution, accompanied by Morten Bergsmo for the prosecution, Mr. Dan Saxon for the Prosecution and Ms. Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am professor Radomir Lukic, proposed by the accused Stakic as accused counsel. The process of my designation as such is still underway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wish to bid welcome to counsel, both for the Prosecution and for the Defence. This Status Conference has been organised to permit the first contact between the parties and the Pre-Trial Judge that has just been designated, and that is myself. As announced by the order of the May 1st, we may also touch upon the question of communication between the parties which, as you know, is crucial for the progress of our work so as to ensure for the accused here present, Mr. Milomir Stakic, a fair and expeditious trial. I would like to suggest for this Status Conference the following agenda. First, we are going to take stock of the situation. Point two, we are going to discuss some general ideas in connection with the preparations of the trial which can help us all to improve our mutual communications. Perhaps we need to synchronise our views with certain procedures. And a third point would be other matters or other business, if you yourself have anything to suggest, and it will be up to you to make such suggestions which will not be connected with the two points that I have mentioned previously, and at the end of the hearing, I will give Mr. Stakic an opportunity to speak. So we come to the first point. For today, I should like to know where we stand as regards the disclosure of the material. You know how important that disclosure is for the pre-trial and I would, in fact, say that the pre-trial can actually begin only once the exhibits have been disclosed in -- pursuant to Rule 66 and 68 and after all the preliminary motions have been addressed pursuant to Article 72, and this is stated by Rule 65 ter. So it is really important to see where we stand, as I was saying, regarding the disclosure of evidence. I should now like to turn to Ms. Susan Somers for her to tell us how we stand in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I had relayed through channels that on Friday last, which would have been 27 April, the Prosecution, in the absence of having counsel upon whom to serve the supporting materials for the original indictment, went to the detention unit and met with Dr. Stakic to try to give him, as the only logical recipient, the materials. It was indicated by Dr. Stakic that he preferred to wait for counsel as he believed would be coming in the next few days, and the investigator therefore unable to deliver to Dr. Stakic the materials, returned them to the Office of the Prosecutor where they are waiting now to be delivered to Professor Lukic. I have, for the record, a declaration by the investigator as to his visit to the Detention Centre and I would simply like to make it a part of the record so as to make it clear that the Prosecutor did try to carry out its obligations but was unable to for reasons peculiar to this particular case. I have checked on a regular basis with the Registry to see if and when counsel for the accused would be assigned so as to try to have a preliminary opportunity to meet with him or her. I am pleased that at last, there is someone with whom I can deal and I have indicated to Professor Lukic that immediately following this hearing I would like to hand him the materials and to have an opportunity to speak with him. I hope I am correct in and permitted to say that he agreed to do the same. The Prosecution as I indicated at this point is proceeding with a disclosure as to only the initial indictment and is in the process of preparing an amended indictment which was indicated to the full Chamber at the first appearance. We will -- we are working diligently and if the Chamber requires, from time to time, a progress report, we are prepared to make it. The Chamber's -- may I ask for a moment of -- for a private session, please. Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question I have has to do with the amendment of the indictment. From the point of view of the pre-trial, I should like to ask you if you can tell us, I'm asking you, from the standpoint of the pre-trial, it is important to know more or less what type of modification the Prosecutor is going to make to the indictment. That is to say, whether the facts are going to be more or less the same and they will be distributed among several counts using different legal qualifications for the same facts or are new facts going to be added? I am putting this question to you because if the facts don't change, and if there is only one legal qualification, we can work and make progress in the pre-trial stage already. But if the Prosecutor is going to add new facts, new material, new evidence, then there will have to be fresh disclosure and that will mean delaying the real beginning of the pre-trial stage. Are you in a position to tell us a little more in response to this question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The indictment will surround, Your Honour, the same essential core of incidents; however, all that is charged, the sole charge now is the genocide. There will be, as was consistent with the previous co-accused, an expansion, based again, on facts that are certainly well centred and known of some, perhaps most, of the charges that appeared in that indictment, and we are looking very carefully at refining. In addition, we have been able, pursuant to those same, essentially the same types of facts and the same situation that prevailed in Prijedor, we have the benefit of material that has come from a number of sources since the original indictment was confirmed, and indeed, since the amendment of Kovacevic and the Drljaca, Kovacevic, Stakic indictment was confirmed. So it will surround events in Prijedor. There will be an expansion as to - which is appropriate - to a policy person, a person who was in the type of role, occupied the type of role as is alleged to have been occupied by Dr. Stakic. And I think at this point, I will not go further, but that -- I think the Chamber has an idea of certainly the types of events in terms of the underlying crime base plus policy and much of which, of course, is an expansion or a clarification with more specificity of the genocide charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Susan Somers. So there are at least two points here that I would like to submit to Professor Radomir Lukic for his consideration and comment, that is the question of the disclosure of evidence, and also what we have just said with respect to the amendment of the indictment. Mr. Lukic, do you have any comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have certain comments to make regarding the explanations given by the Prosecution. It seems to me that the explanation given by Prosecution counsel is such that it is not possible to decipher what exactly the Prosecution is preparing so that the Defence, at this point in time, finds itself in a rather vague and unfavorable position for it is not clear whether only the genocide charge will remain. What is clear is that there will be new facts which further complicates this stage of our proceedings. Therefore, it seems to me that the Prosecution should, in somewhat greater detail, give us indications as to what it intends to do regarding the expansion of the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Lukic, regarding the disclosure of evidence, have you any comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is ready to receive what the Prosecution is ready to disclose at this point in time, and to act accordingly. However, the Defence realises that things will be complicated with the disclosure of new facts as a result of the expansion of the indictment which complicates our pre-trial work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Before giving the floor to Ms. Susan Somers, I think that in -- up to a point, she has clarified things because my concern was, indeed, to know what would be the impact on the pre-trial stage of any modifications. Ms. Susan Somers mentioned the indictment against Milan Kovacevic and Simo Drljaca, at least the Kovacevic indictment is well known. It was amended. It was the same indictment. I think we can speak about that now. It was an indictment against three accused, one of whom was Milomir Stakic, a second was Kovacevic and the third Simo Drljaca so the situation will repeat itself in a sense, and that is why I asked the Prosecutor whether the modifications consisted of new facts or not. If there are new facts, then there can be an impact on the pre-trial preparations if we are talking about the same facts, but distributed or qualified in a slightly different manner, then that does not have any impact because maybe now I will be generalising, but I think both from the point of view of the Prosecution and the Defence, the pre-trial work, that is my opinion and my view, is work that differs from the trial -- the work after the opening of trial. Therefore, for the pre-trial stage is to discuss the points of fact and law with the view to achieving an agreement on disagreements. In other words, what is the actual object of the trial, what will be the purpose of the trial, because there will be a whole series of facts and law that we are agreed on, that are accepted. So that will not be the object of the proceedings. So when I say that we need to reach agreement on disagreements, it is really a question of defining the subject of the discussions we are going to have throughout the trial. So it is with that in mind that I put this question, and the most important information given to us by Ms. Susan Somers is that the facts that are going to serve as a basis of the amended indictment are already present in the indictment with a single charge. But to confirm that, and perhaps to provide additional clarifications that Professor Lukic needs, I would like to give the floor to Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there have been a number of cases before the various Chambers of this Tribunal and there are, indeed, a number of cases presently before the various Chambers concerning the events in Prijedor as well as the impact of said events generally on the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole. I would be unable and unwilling at this time to go much beyond what I have said, however, the explanation as set forth in the genocide count indicates that it did not happen overnight, that there were factors that occurred in the implementation of whatever policy would be further expanded in the amended indictment. I think this is evident in the Kovacevic Drljaca indictment that had been confirmed. We would be looking, so that there is a better understanding of the direction, at counts perhaps of grave breaches, crimes against humanity and war crimes in addition to the genocide count. Again, these, by understanding the base which this -- the Chamber has had a tremendous amount of contact with and understanding of, these are the essential -- this is the core and from this core, we will find the appropriate charges and we will put the appropriate charges in the amended indictment. I am turning over, of course, a copy of the original Drljaca, Kovacevic -- sorry, before I say the date, let me make sure I'm correct, of the 13 March 1997 confirmed indictment which should give some guidance, I believe, to Mr. Lukic as to the sum of the nature of the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, do you wish to ask for any further clarification or are you happy for the moment with what you have just heard?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the time being, conditionally speaking, I could perhaps be happy with what the counsel for the Prosecution has just said. However, there is one condition, the Defence is going to proceed on the basis of the first indictment, and on the first batch of supporting material while we wait for the expansion of the indictment. At that moment, we will have to adjust ourselves with respect to the new elements in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Because we have indicated a clear intent and are moving in the direction of amendment, I would ask the Chamber to consider that the normal preliminary motions that are filed perhaps be held in abeyance pending the amended indictment simply because of the amount of energy that would have to be expanded on both sides and certainly the requirements that would be upon the Chamber as well. Whereas, we will begin the -- the process has been undertaken. I think if the Rule 72 motions were now set in motion, it would be -- it would require a relitigation of effectively the same motions at a later date and if the Chamber is minded to hold in abeyance that process, mindful of whatever time limits normally would be required pending confirmation of the amended indictment, it may prove to be judicially economical as well as economical from the stand point of energy expanded by counsel on both sides. I believe that in the amendment of the Kordic indictment there was a similar request that had been made and the motions, if my memory serves me correctly, were held after the amended indictment. I can check that, but it strikes me that that was the case because it was clear that there would be -- and the dual effort seemed wasteful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that raises another issue. When do you intend to submit the amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Without being firmly bound because of the way we are proceeding, I would hope by the end of the summer, and that is working at a consistent pace. We are analysing and documenting material and -- to make sure that we have everything in one round rather than have to return to the Chamber. We want to make sure that it is judicially economically done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what exactly you mean when you say by the end of the summer. Could you be more precise, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We have, as a target, between the middle and end of July. That is a target date subject to any complications that may arise, but that would be our goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, do you wish to make a comment on what we have just heard from Ms. Somers, that is, that preliminary motions pursuant to Article 72 be held in abeyance pending the submission of the amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the application of Rule 72 and the motions to be held in abeyance maybe it would make sense at this point and in the interest of both the work of the Defence and the Prosecution. I can give you my agreement in principle, however, the issue should be dealt with cautiously and prudently when it comes to the behaviour of the Prosecution in terms of dates, deadlines, and materials that we are supposed to receive pursuant to the amended indictment because that aspect of the problem can have a significant impact on the preparation of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I should now hear Mr. Lukic in respect of certain clarifications. If that beginning of the proceedings is depending on the Prosecutor, who has a number of obligations to fulfil, if we have a look at the relevant provisions regarding the pre-trial proceedings, I think that we can now distinguish two stages of the proceedings, the pre-trial phase of the Prosecution and then after the Prosecution rests, there would be a pre-trial proceedings for the Defence case. As regards that second -- as regards the pre-trial proceedings of the Prosecution, it is the Rule 65 ter (E) and (F) which provide for the measures to be taken. That is to say, it is expected of the Defence to participate in that part of the preliminary proceedings in order to state in general terms the nature of the accused Defence, the matters with which the accused takes issues in the Prosecutor's pre-trial brief and so on and so forth as provided for by the Rule. That is to say, we have to find an agreement on disagreement, that is on matters in dispute. However, there are other obligations on the part of the Defence and I should like to hear Mr. Lukic once again, if you can perhaps tell us at this juncture whether you intend to submit any preliminary motions at all and if you intend to invoke Rule 66(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Sometimes it is referred to reciprocal disclosure between the parties. This Rule needs to be considered in light of Rule 67(C). So whether you can tell us at this point whether you intend to present a Defence of alibi or any special defence such as provided for by Rule 67. So, Mr. Lukic, if you have a general idea, without committing yourself one way or another, I should like to hear you regarding the provisions that I have just quoted and these suggestions that I have just made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope that you will be able to understand that at this point in time, I am really not in a position to give you a precise answer whereby I would take it upon myself to abide by what I say here. I was only informed on Friday about the request of Mr. Stakic about my designation and I was invited to participate in the Status Conference on the same day. Everything happened very fast, and I really had no time to think about these issues. However, I proceed with full responsibility before this honorable Tribunal and I will endeavour to inform this Chamber about the issues that have just been made as soon as I am able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. We do understand your position. As regards the issue of abeyance of preliminary motions, I think that it is appropriate to proceed that way since we all have to wait for the amended indictment. However, my objective was to complete the pre-trial proceedings at the end of October, but I don't think that preliminary motions prevent us from working in terms of facts, factual issues during this pre-trial stage. But you're quite right, I hereby decide to extend the deadline for the submission of preliminary motions, that is, to hold them in abeyance once this future Initial Appearance is held pursuant to the amended indictment, and only then are we going to hear you on preliminary motions. Which brings me to the second point, second item on our agenda for today. That is, the procedures to be applied during the pre-trial proceedings. If you read the Rule 65 ter, you will see that the condition, the requirement which enable us to work during this preliminary phase of the proceedings is the completion of the disclosure of evidence and the decisions pursuant to Rule 72. However, I don't think that we have -- that we can start with the preliminary proceedings without these requirements being met. However, I think that we can proceed with matters of dispute and matters not in dispute when it comes to facts. Because one of the objectives of the pre-trial stage of the proceedings is something that is announced, that is envisaged here in Sub-rule (E) of Rule 65 ter, that is, we have to know what is exactly the case of the Prosecution, what are the matters which are not in dispute, and also what are the contested matters of facts and law. This should constitute the first step that we have to take in this pre-trial proceedings. Once we are aware of what the case actually is, we will be in the position to define and streamline the evidence which will bring us to the second stage of the preliminary proceedings, that is, the list of witnesses and everything else that is contained in Item 4 of that Sub-rule. There are several, therefore, stages of this preliminary phase, and we can also discuss the issue of the order of presentation of evidence in the courtroom, witnesses, video material, affidavits, and so on and so forth. Once we deal with that issue, we will be in the third stage of the proceedings, that is, the issue of exhibits. At Item 5 of Sub-rule (E), that, is the list of exhibits the Prosecutor intends to offer stating wherever possible whether the Defence has any objection as to their authenticity. So I think that we can also deal at that time with the issue of expert witnesses. I have, therefore, identified three stages of our work and I don't think that there is anything that is preventing us from proceeding with these issues, that is, the fact that we still do not have an amended indictment, and that the preliminary motions haven't yet been dealt with. That, I don't think, hinders us in any way in terms of steps and procedures that are envisaged in Sub-rule (E) of Rule 65 ter; that is, we should discuss the issues of matters of dispute and not in dispute. I have to say at this point, Mr. Lukic, that we should not be invoking the case law of the Tribunal at this point. There are always precedents and we do not have a firmly-established case law on all of these issues. If there is an appeal, the merits should be discussed later on. But be that as it may, I do believe that we can proceed with certain practical matters during this pre-trial stage of the proceedings, so I invite you to start working on the amended indictment and let us have it as soon as possible. Afterwards, we will be dealing with the preliminary motions, but at the same time in parallel, we can, I think, proceed with the work regarding the indictment that we already have in terms of facts, because as we have heard, the facts will remain more or less the same. So certain aspects of the work can already begin. As you know, at the Plenary Sessions, the Judges have adopted a number of provisions regarding the preliminary stage of the proceedings and I believe that the said provisions enter into force today. The Chamber has already applied those provisions in another case so we do have some experience with these procedures which provide for the trial judge to be able to participate in a more active way in this stage so that once the trial begins, it can go on as fast as possible and as efficiently as possible. First of all, we have to have a work plan on the basis of which we can proceed. Let me try to explain to you what I understand by work plan. Any such work plan should have its objectives and appropriate methodology. The objectives are provided for in Rule 65 ter, Sub-rule (E) for the Prosecution and Sub-rule (F) for the Defence. There is a methodology that goes with that objective and I believe that this methodology is more or less the same mutatis mutandis as the methodology of Rule 71 and the statements taken by a presiding officer. It is one of the general ideas in terms of methodology. However, there is another aspect of this issue of methodology and that is the efficient use of time. In this Chamber, we have so far been applying a methodology in terms of adequate use of time and space. It is very important for the parties to be able to meet with each other and it is also very important that the parties are also close in terms of space and that they have adequate possibility to meet in order to discuss and analyse the issues which only later on will come before the Judges and will be discussed in the courtroom. Once those issues are discussed in the courtroom, the parties have to meet once again and see whether any progress, further progress can be made and then after that, of course, they come back to the Judges and inform them about the progress. We have to have meetings. They can take place here in the courtroom. They can also take place in my office or in the office of the senior legal officer of the Chambers and I think that we will have -- that we will achieve good results by applying this methodology of work. So as I have just indicated, the work plan will be elaborated in light of this perspective. We have to define the objectives and the methodology. You can avail yourselves of the presence of the legal officer, of the Chamber who is also presiding officer in some cases, in order to discuss the issues. So in order -- we have to try to organise the Pre-Trial Conference as soon as possible, but that means that we will have to go through a number of stages that I have already identified. The first stage being to reach agreement on the issues identified in Sub-rule (E) of Rule 65 ter. The second stage concerns item 4 of Sub-rule (E), that is, the list of witnesses or rather the presentation of evidence in different forms in which it can be called. And finally, the third stage being the list of exhibits including, if possible, if any, any expert witness reports. So those would be the three stages which will enable us to work. The first one, once again, being trying to find an agreement on matters of dispute, and not in dispute. However, we have to see what evidence we will have to deal with in terms of material and documents that the Prosecutor intends to present and what are, in general terms, the main -- what will be, in general terms, the Defence case. So I have just identified a number of tasks for you so that you can start working during this preliminary phase of the proceedings. It is essential that the parties meet, and I said that we will do so, but the parties also may do so on their own initiative. As has already been decided as Rule 65(D) authorises me to do, that the legal officer of the Chamber, Mr. Olivier Fourmy, to assist me in the pre-trial proceedings of this case. It will be up to him to see with you, to consider the questions that need to be addressed and to keep me informed should any difficulties arise. And there, I see a comparison with the system of evidence by depositions because the presiding officer is delegated by the Chamber. In this case, he assists the Pre-Trial Judge. He monitors the implementation of the work plan, but he must always communicate to the Pre-Trial Judge any difficulties that may arise and keep constantly in touch with him so that he can follow the progress of the preparations. So you can ask him to organise a meeting, and also he may request a meeting with you, that is, the Prosecution, the Defence separately or together. Proceeding in this way, I hope that we will relatively speedily come to a point when the trial can begin towards the end of October or -- because or rather that the pre-trial phase be completed by October. That is our target. If you calculate the time limits in the Rules, you will see that the pre-trial stage has to be completed in more or less six months. We have started now, but I think that we can complete this stage towards the end of October. I say this because as you know, the Judges that now constitute this Chamber will not remain as of November. But we would like to complete our work before then. Therefore, it is the duty of this Chamber to prepare this case, and we would like to achieve that. It is up to the Chamber to do its work, and we are determined to do so. I am saying this so that we might all achieve this objective of the pre-trial proceedings. We will see what we can do. In any event, I should like to give you a chance to present your views or remarks or questions regarding what I have just said with regard to the new rule of the pre-trial proceedings, the plan of work and the methodology I have presented. I should like to hear your reactions. Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution will of course remain mindful of the timeframe the Chamber has pronounced. I would also ask that the Chamber encourage the use of judicially noticed facts which the Chamber has so wisely allowed us to use in other cases. I think that it is a mechanism which will save potentially months of litigation and works, I believe, to the advantage of all parties and in the interests of justice. Adjudicated facts, as well as, which may form the basis of notice should be brought to the attention of the Chamber from -- as they become appropriate after completion of all phases of other trials which may have bearing on this case. The issue which haunts every Chamber and Prosecution, of course, is the need to bring in the same witnesses over and over again because of the way accused come before the Tribunal perhaps serially delivered or perhaps because of the way cases are broken up. And I would ask the Chamber also to assist us in encouraging mechanisms that will not require unnecessary burdens, where appropriate, on certain witnesses to come in again and again. There are pending, besides the Omarska case, the Keraterm case, the Talic/Brdjanin case, and this case matters before various Chambers that have of necessity repetition of witnesses and I would ask this Chamber to assist us in not encouraging witness burn-out or failure of witnesses to appear because of the repeated necessity of so doing. I want to state that I am available to counsel for the Defence any time he needs or wishes to see me, subject to my obligations in court or with my office, and I maintain an open-door policy. I do want to indicate that we did try to reach out as early as possible, and unfortunately because of some red tape, we were unable to make contact but we will make every effort to meet regularly as has been our practice in the other case before this Chamber, and to try to reduce issues to the minimum so that we can get on with the case. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, with respect to the work plan regarding objectives and methodology, have you a word to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that it is a very sound plan. I realise that a certain part of our work will be held up a bit because of the amendment, but I agree fully that there are things that we can tackle now that we should, indeed, begin to tackle now because when we are in full swing, it will require our full energy. So yes, I think it's very sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Ms. Susan Somers. Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic, have you any comments, remarks, or questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the plan that you have set out may give us hope that the trial will proceed as expeditiously as necessary so as to reach the actual trial stage. We are ready to cooperate with you and the Prosecution to that end, and as regards time limits, I hope that with your assistance, we will be able to observe them. The question just raised by the Prosecution, that is, the question of adjudicated facts and the status of witnesses that have to appear in several cases, in my view, are of a principle nature, and the Defence is unable to take a position with that regard at this stage yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. I would like to tell you that the concern of this Chamber have already been implemented in the cases that are ongoing before this Chamber. We have prepared trials, and I can tell you that in one particular case, we achieved excellent results by a simple reading of the indictment by the two parties and the Pre-Trial Judge. We read together the indictment going through it and everyone saying, "I agree. I do not agree. I am totally in agreement. I am partially in disagreement." So it is possible to reach stipulations on the basis of the indictment and I accept that. Why, because at the end, there will be a whole series of facts that you will see in the indictment that have nothing to do with the person of Milomir Stakic himself. It has to do with history, the description of a conflict, the general background, but what is important, in my opinion, for the Defence, and I would ask the Defence to adopt an active Defence role, an attitude I do wish to discuss these matters. Because very often, Defence counsel take a passive attitude. It is up to the Prosecution to prove things and I will just wait. However, as you know, in the language of football, defensive teams as a rule lose the match. So it is important to attack to win. So a good position to be taken by the Defence is a dynamic position, a position of communicating with the other party and an active, committed attitude. I do wish to discuss, and to go into the details. So what I think is really important for the Defence is everything that really affects the responsibility of the accused. There are other things that are of a general nature that provide the context, the framework. So in that regard, we can move forward. And in the other case, we did make progress because there was judicial notice, partly judicial notice and partly stipulations, on the basis of some 500 facts. Out of those 500, some 440 were accepted as adjudicated. So this enormously facilitates the process of witnesses, the exhibits and so on. Now, as regards this case, we have at least the Omarska case that is related, the Keraterm case. We have the Talic and Brdjanin case, then we have the Kovacevic case too, to a certain extent. So there are many things, in my view, which have already been cleared up to a point and it is possible to negotiate on condition that they do not concern the responsibility of the accused. There is something else that has to be borne in mind. Since we have all these different cases, there is also a large number of witnesses who have already appeared here in court and, in my opinion, it is not useful, in the interest of justice, for the parties or for the Tribunal to make a witness come back to repeat what he has already said and which has been recorded in a transcript of which we have audio and visual record. So I think that one should accept that there is one particular point that this witness needs to clarify because this may be a point that another Defence counsel had not raised because his Defence strategy was different because he forgot or for any other reason. But if there is a real reason to have a witness brought back, we shall do so, but only to tell us something new. If he is to say what he has already said, that has no sense. Therefore, I think that we must be reasonable and, for instance, one could imagine a video conference for the case of a witness who has already appeared in the Tribunal, who has already made his testimony before the Judges after taking the solemn declaration. But if there is one question with the Defence counsel or the Prosecution wishes to put to him, then for that one question, the witness can answer that question by video conferencing, avoiding his travel here, wasting a lot of time bringing him here to the courtroom to give an answer to one single question. So you see, there is a whole series of issues from the practical point of view that we will address, but at this stage of the beginning of the pre-trial, perhaps we need to share them with you already so that the parties may reflect upon them and give them thought. I think that we are all keen on the trial being expeditious but also fair or, vice versa, the trial should be fair but also expeditious. So that is the balance that we wish to build as from now. I should now like to go on to the third point of the agenda, and that is other business or other questions. Are there any other questions which have not been addressed and which should be addressed now? I am looking at Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I cannot think of anything procedurally that you have not covered, Your Honour. I -- again, after I have a chance to speak with Mr. Lukic after the session has ended there may be something, and I will inform your officer if that's appropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Ms. Susan Somers. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, at this point in time, Your Honour, I have no question that I feel needs to be addressed just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was just reminded, this may be absolutely superfluous, but because this is the first time I have we've had dealings with each other, of course the materials which will be given out as supporting materials are confidential and we have attached a receipt which indicates their confidential nature and that they are not to be disclosed to anyone. I just wanted to inform the Chamber that we have so included this caveat. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am going to issue the work plan and a few guidelines with respect to the objectives and methodology and especially scheduling formally designating Mr. Olivier Fourmy as the legal officer who will assist me in this pre-trial proceedings establishing the role that he will play, but from this moment on, you are able to communicate through him with me. I should like to give him the floor to see whether he has anything to add for this Status Conference. Mr. Olivier Fourmy.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Thank you very much for the confidence shown in me, and by the Chamber through you in designating me as a person who could facilitate the pre-trial stage of these proceedings, and I should like to invite the parties to contact me, either separately or together, whenever they feel the need to do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much, Mr. Olivier Fourmy. There is something I would like to address before I give the floor to Dr. Stakic. That is the composition of Mr. Lukic's team. I think to be able to develop their work and to be able to fulfil our objectives in terms of the schedule, we really have to pay attention to this and I am referring to the composition of Mr. Lukic's team. I should like to ask Madam Registrar where we stand with respect to that issue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I just spoke with Chritain Rohde this morning and he informed me that a decision a being made now to make Mr. Lukic counsel for Mr. Stakic. And as far as getting more people for his team, Mr. Lukic will have to ask Mr. Rohde for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So Mr. Lukic, you have an additional task, and that is to form your team and to communicate with Mr. Christian Rohde so that the team could be constituted because we wouldn't like to hear you say tomorrow that you were not able to complete your work because you were alone, you have no co-counsel and no proper team. I have made this remark to the Registry so that the Registry take care of your requests so that the Registrar should be well aware of our interest in working properly and completing our work by October. And in order to achieve that, it is also important for the Registrar to provide the necessary resources for you to compose your team. Before adjourning this hearing, I should like to address Dr. Stakic. Will you stand, please. I should like to ask you whether there is anything in particular that you would like to say, specifically regarding conditions of detention and your health. Are you feeling well? Do you have anything to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that you know that I have been operated on 14 or 15 days ago and, thank God, and thanks to the doctors, my colleagues who did a good job, I am already feeling quite well. The wound is healing and I hope everything will be fine and thank you for your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, after this first meeting, we will really be able to begin establishing a good cooperative strategy, a strategy from which all of us will gain, the accused, the Defence, the Prosecution, the Chamber, and justice in general. It is not a case when somebody gains and the other loses. It really is something that all can benefit from if making the proper contribution. So I encourage you to adopt such a working perspective, because when somebody does not cooperate, it makes the overall task more complicated. So I think the spirit of cooperation and communication can make the work of all of us easier, simpler, but also more effective and more beneficial. Having made that remark, I wish to say that I am very happy to work with you. I am always available through Mr. Olivier Fourmy, and we will do everything we can to complete the pre-trial stage by October so that the trial can begin as soon as possible. Thank you for your attention. Success in your work. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon The Status Conference is adjourned at
